answer: Mechanism: Entropy-Priced Pulse Routing (EPPR). Agents publish a knoll—their local coordination neighborhood—in a shared atlas. Each pulse, the router charges for cross-knoll fanout plus the Shannon entropy of action signatures in that pulse. Identical signatures are deduplicated to one effective action; distinct signatures raise the toll. An attacker wanting N sybils to count must either pay for N distinct signatures and cross-knoll routes, or collapse them and lose amplification. Cost scales with coordination entropy, not identity count.
